guides.title: Why a cold bedroom beats a warm one for sleep
guides.dek: Core temperature has to fall for deep sleep to start. That is physiology, not preference.
body: Sleep onset is triggered by a drop in core temperature of roughly half a degree. A room at 23C keeps you at the top of your thermal window, so the drop never arrives and you lie there awake.
The fix is not a colder room — most people hate that. It is taking heat away from the head and neck, which is where a body dumps heat fastest because the blood vessels there sit close to the surface.
A breathable, phase-change or gel pad under the head does that passively. It needs no electricity, no timer, and nothing to remember at 3am.
Two things matter when choosing one: the fill has to move heat rather than insulate, and the cover has to be washable, because a pillow you cannot wash stops being a pillow.

guides.title: How often a kettle actually needs descaling
guides.dek: Hard water areas: every four to six weeks. Soft water: every three months. Never 'when it looks bad'.
body: Limescale is calcium carbonate. It insulates the element, so a scaled kettle takes longer to boil and pulls more current for the same cup — the cost shows up on the bill before the kettle dies.
Descale with citric acid, not vinegar. Citric rinses clean in one pass; vinegar leaves an acetic tang that taints the next three brews.
Half fill, two tablespoons of citric acid, boil, stand twenty minutes, rinse twice, then boil fresh water once and pour it away.
If your area is above 200mg/l hardness, treat four weeks as the interval and put it in the calendar rather than trusting your memory.

guides.title: Getting the cash out of a scuffed car park
guides.dek: Two scuffs and a kerbed alloy will cost more at resale than a full detail. Fix them or the buyer discounts twice over.
body: Trade-in valuations dock around 120 to 200 pounds for visible paint damage, and the deduction is applied per panel rather than per mark.

A scratch that you cannot feel with a fingernail is in the clearcoat and will usually polish out. If it catches your nail, it needs touch-up paint before polishing, or the pad just rounds the edges of the gouge.
Work in shade on a cool panel, and finish with a sealant — bare polished clearcoat oxidises faster than the paint around it, so an unsealed repair looks worse in a month.
Alloy kerbing is the one to leave to a mobile repairer unless the wheel is bare metal and uncoated.

guides.title: Walking a dog in horizontal rain without a wet car
guides.dek: The towel lives by the door, not in the cupboard. That one change does more than any gadget.
body: A dog shakes roughly 70% of the water off in the first second after a wet walk, and most of it lands within two metres of the door. Position decides whether that is the porch or the boot.
Microfibre stow towels absorb more per gram and dry faster than cotton; cotton hangs damp for hours and smells of the walk.
Dry legs and belly first, then the back against the grain. A clip torch on the lead keeps you visible on the dark side of the lane, which is the part people forget when buying for rain.
